title: Study on Changes in Serum Biomarkers in Different Stages of Pancreatic Cancer
projectDescription: By studying the serum proteins of patients with pancreatic cancer at different stages, we aim to identify secreted factors that influence tumor progression in pancreatic cancer.
sampleProcessingProtocol: 1. Protein Extraction Collect whole blood into a vacuum collection vessel and gently mix by inverting it 5-6 times. Place the vessel at 4 °C for 45 minutes, then centrifuge at 1300 g for 10 minutes at 4 °C. Transfer the upper serum to a centrifuge tube using a pipette, immediately add a protease inhibitor, mix well, and centrifuge at 1300 g briefly. First, cellular debris from the serum sample was removed by centrifugation at 12,000 g at 4 °C for 10 minutes. The supernatant was then transferred to a new centrifuge tube. Finally, the protein concentration was determined using a BCA kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.  2. Trypsin Digestion Initially, the serum samples were removed with a high-abundant proteins via Thermo kit (A36369, Thermo). The solution was treated with 5 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) for 30 minutes at 56 °C and then alkylated with 11 mM iodoacetamide (IAM) for 15 minutes at room temperature in the dark. Next, 70 μL of enzyme digestion buffer was added to the beads and incubated at 95 °C for 10 minutes, allowing the samples to return to room temperature. Trypsin was then added to a final concentration of 20 ng/μL for overnight digestion. The resulting peptides were desalted using C18 ZipTips (Millipore) according to the manufacturer’s instructions and then dried for subsequent MS analysis.  3. LC-MS/MS Analysis The tryptic peptides were dissolved in solvent A and directly loaded onto a home-made reversed-phase analytical column (15-cm length, 100 μm i.d.). The mobile phase consisted of solvent A (0.1% formic acid in water) and solvent B (0.1% formic acid, 80% acetonitrile in water). Peptides were separated with the following gradient: 0-1.6 min, 4%-22.5% B; 1.6-2.0 min, 22.5%-35% B; 2.0-2.6 min, 35%-55% B; 2.6-2.7 min, 55%-99% B; 2.7-6.8 min, 99% B; 6.8-7.6 min, 99% B, all at a constant flow rate of 300 nl/min on a Vanquish Neo UPLC system (ThermoFisher Scientific). The separated peptides were analyzed using an Orbitrap Astral with a nano-electrospray ion source. The electrospray voltage applied was 1900 V. Precursorswere analyzed at the Orbitrap detector, and the fragments were analyzed at the Astral detector. The full MS scan resolution was set to 240,000 for a scan range of 380-980 m/z. The MS/MS scan was set to a fixed first mass of 150.0 m/z at a resolution of 80,000. HCD fragmentation was performed at a normalized collision energy (NCE) of 25%. The automatic gain control (AGC) target was set at 500%, with a maximum injection time of 3 ms.
dataProcessingProtocol: The DIA data were processed using the DIA-NN search engine (v.1.8). Tandem mass spectra were searched against the Homo_sapiens_9606_SP_20231220.fasta database (20,429 entries) concatenated with a reverse decoy database. Trypsin/P was specified as the cleavage enzyme, allowing up to 1 missed cleavage. N-terminal Met excision and carbamidomethylation of Cys were specified as fixed modifications. The false discovery rate (FDR) was adjusted to <1%.
